title: Evaluation of the Measurement Accuracy of an AI-Based Measurement System (SCALE-EYE) for Determining Polyp Size During Colonoscopies in Individuals with Lynch Syndrome
summary: Lynch syndrome (LS) is the most common hereditary cause of colorectal cancer (CRC). The condition is caused by germline mutations in specific DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes—including MLH1, MSH2/EPCAM, MSH6, and PMS2—which normally repair DNA replication errors. In the absence of preventive measures, affected individuals carry a significantly elevated lifetime risk of developing colorectal cancer (up to 70–80% for MLH1/MSH2 carriers). Consequently, regular surveillance colonoscopy is mandatory and is recommended every one to two years starting at an early age, depending on genotype and family history. The primary objective of colonoscopy is the detection and, where feasible, immediate removal of polyps.  Polyps are widely recognized as precursor lesions of colorectal cancer. They are stratified based on their respective risk of malignant transformation, with polyp size serving as the decisive risk factor. The 10 mm threshold is of particular clinical relevance; the presence of one or more adenomas ≥10 mm leads to classification into the high-risk surveillance group. Furthermore, the choice of endoscopic resection method is guided by polyp size. Diminutive polyps or flat mucosal lesions are typically removed via cold snare polypectomy (i.e., without the application of electrical current), whereas larger polyps about 1 cm or more are resected using hot snare polypectomy. Therefore, misclassification of polyp size has direct and clinically significant consequences. Underestimating lesions  ≥ 10 mm can delay post-polypectomy surveillance and increase the risk of advanced neoplasia or interval cancers (cancers arising between scheduled screening examinations). Conversely, overestimating smaller lesions may result in an unnecessary shortening of surveillance intervals, repeated procedures, increased patient burden, and avoidable healthcare costs.
conditions: Familial colorectal cancer (Lynch syndrome) / colorectal adenomas

interventions.name: Experimental intervention: Polyp size measurement during colonoscopy using SCALE-EYE (FUJIFILM, CE-certified).
Control intervention: Conventional, snare-based visual estimation of polyp size during colonoscopy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Written consent from the participant to voluntarily participate in the study
•    The participant’s ability to follow the study instructions and expected participation in all required study visits
Indication-specific inclusion criteria:
•    Diagnosis of Lynch syndrome (evidence of a (probably) pathogenic germline variant in MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, or PMS2; or a deletion in the 3′ region of the EPCAM gene)
•    Scheduled surveillance colonoscopy
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion Criteria: 
General Exclusion Criteria:

•    Participants who lack legal capacity and are unable to understand the nature, scope, significance, and consequences of this study

•    Patients with physical or psychiatric conditions or systemic diseases that, in the investigator’s judgment,
o    could jeopardize the participant’s safety
o    could distort the study results,
o    could interfere with participation in the study, 
o    could prevent adequate compliance

  Exclusion criteria regarding specific restrictions for women:
•    Current pregnancy

  Indication-specific exclusion criteria:
•    Concomitant inflammatory bowel disease (e.g., Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis)
